title.en: Refraction, dispersion and scattering of light

text.en: On a clear day the sky is blue but at sunset the Sun turns red. A glass prism turns white light into a rainbow band. All of this is explained by how light bends and scatters when it meets matter.

When light travels obliquely from one transparent medium into another it changes direction; this bending is called refraction and it happens because the speed of light is different in the two media.
Light is faster in a rarer medium and slower in a denser medium, and when it goes from a denser to a rarer medium it bends away from the normal.
The first law of refraction says that the incident ray, the refracted ray and the normal all lie in the same plane.
The second law, Snell's law, says that sin i divided by sin r is equal to the ratio of the refractive indices of the two media.
The refractive index of a medium is n = c / v, the speed of light in vacuum divided by its speed in the medium, so a high n means slow light.
White light is a composite light; when it passes through a prism it splits into the seven colours VIBGYOR, a band called the spectrum, and this is dispersion.
Dispersion happens because each colour has a different refractive index: red bends the least and violet bends the most.
Scattering is the redirection of light in all directions by atoms, molecules or particles of the medium called scatterers.
Rayleigh's law says the amount of scattering is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength, so blue scatters much more than red and the sky looks blue.
At sunrise and sunset the sunlight travels a longer path, most of the blue is scattered away and the red reaches us, so the Sun looks red; large scatterers like dust and water droplets cause Mie scattering, which does not depend on wavelength, so clouds look white.

problem.en: The speed of light in vacuum is 3 x 10^8 m/s and in glass it is 2 x 10^8 m/s. Find the refractive index of glass. A ray in air strikes the glass at i = 30 degrees; find the angle of refraction.

text.en: Snell's law from air (n = 1) to glass: sin i / sin r = 1.5 / 1.
sin r = sin 30 / 1.5 = 0.5 / 1.5 = 0.333, so r is about 19.5 degrees.

why.en: The ray bends towards the normal because glass is denser.

text.en: Since r is smaller than i, the ray moved towards the normal.

prompt.en: Explain why the sky is blue and the setting Sun is red.

requiredIdeas.en: Rayleigh scattering is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength
Blue has a shorter wavelength so it is scattered more
At sunset the light travels a longer path, blue is scattered away and red reaches us

commonMisconceptions.en: Blue light is created in the sky
The sky reflects the colour of the sea

points.en: n = c / v; light bends towards the normal entering a denser medium.
Snell's law: sin i / sin r = n2 / n1.
Dispersion gives VIBGYOR: red bends least, violet most.
Rayleigh: scattering is proportional to 1 / wavelength to the power 4, hence the blue sky and red sunset.
